Mission: Taobao's "Online Pharmacy Pilot" & The Rise of Early Gray Markets
Description: Merchants bypassed platform audits using coded product names, making e-commerce platforms like Taobao the primary battleground for the trans community to source HRT medications. This gave rise to an increasingly sophisticated "code-word purchasing" network.

Mission: Ban on E-Commerce Pharmacy Pilots & Regulatory Backlash
Description: Authorities suspended online third-party prescription drug sales, leading to widespread store closures on e-commerce platforms. The community was forced to turn to far more fragmented gray channels.

Standard HRT medications were not included in the list of "prohibited special-controlled drugs," obtaining HRT through online hospitals became exceptionally convenient for those without an existing prescription.

Mission: NMPA Explicitly Defines Scope of Prohibited Online Retail Drugs
Description: Injectable estrogen medication were put under strict control, and the variety of available formulations and types of online HRT medications was drastically reduced.

The loop of purchasing prescription drugs without a prior prescription was completely broken: individuals without an official diagnosis of gender dysphoria/transsexuality from a offline Grade 3A hospital could no longer buy prescription drugs online.

Mission: NMPA Further Tightens Platform Compliance Standards
Description: The possibility of internet hospitals using "automated/AI electronic prescription generation" was thoroughly shut down. HRT access shifted entirely back to offline Grade 3A hospital outpatient systems, placing trans individuals who lack family support, cannot secure an offline diagnosis, or live in medically underserved areas in unprecedented access hardship.
